newsitem.title: USA: Peru needs strategy to boost exports - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Peru needs strategy to boost exports - analysts.

text.p: Peru will likely stay its course of economic policy, but the country must adopt a long-term strategy to diversify its exports and strengthen its political institututions, analysts said Tuesday.

"I see no major deviation in the short-, medium- or long-term from sensible macroeconomic policies," said political analyst Francisco Sagasti, director of Agenda: Peru. "No one wants to go back to populism."

Sagasti, speaking at an Americas Society panel here, said the country should devise an strategy similar to the vibrant Asian economies to find the "right balance" of state and market forces to boost export earnings.
"What we need to do is use the boom to diversify exports," Sagasti said, noting that the constitution of Peru's exports has changed little over the past 30 years.

Pedro-Pablo Kuczynski, president of the Latin American Enterprise, said he saw "no real obstacle" for Peru to elevate exports to $15 billion per year by boosting industries such as fishing, agriculture and assembly products.
Last week, Peru reported that its exports for the first nine months of 1996 stood at $4.36 billion.
"We have to foster in Peru an export mentality," Kuczynski said. "Unless we double our exports in four years, the debt burden will drag down growth.
Peru also suffers from an overconcentration of power in the executive branch of government, with four cabinet ministries controlling 80 percent of the budget, Sagasti said.
The problem would be exacerbated should President Alberto Fujimori be reelected to a third term in 2000, he said.
"There is a need for a transition that brackets Fujimori to two terms," Sagasti said.
